verdicts.evidence: On Gaussian/exponential kernels in 2D/3D/5D (n=80–120), the Sinkhorn iteration drives row-sum error to ~1e-13 and mass-weighted self-adjointness relative error to ~1e-16 or 0.0; mutations breaking symmetry or using row normalization raise the error to 1e-2–3e-1, confirming the test is discriminating.

Sup-norm errors of T_N f − T_ref f decrease monotonically with clean algebraic rates (1D: ~2.0, 2D: ~1.0–1.3) for both Gaussian and exponential kernels on [0,1] and [0,1]^2 across increasing resolutions; the sign-oscillating kernel mutation causes divergence, confirming positivity is load-bearing.

Across 40 configurations (n=200, dims 2/3, multiple bandwidths and mass types), iteration counts to reach <0.1% error are min 6, median 9.5, max 11, with 90% landing in the 5–10 window; the extreme-mass-range mutation needing 14 iterations is honestly reported as a boundary case.

The Sinkhorn operator scores 4/4 properties (symmetry err ~1e-16, mass err ~1e-12, positive, spectrum in [0,1]) and baselines score 3/4 and 2/4 against a prescribed mass, but row normalization evaluated against its own degree measure also achieves 4/4 (sym err 2.2e-16, mass err 4.4e-16), a concrete counter-example to the exclusivity sub-clause.

All three data types show Laplacian-like behavior (Dirichlet energy decay, monotone damping, constant annihilation) on real runs, but the jaw-bone voxel scan is replaced by a synthetic 24³ sparse shell and the GMM uses n=300, so the paper's actual assets and Section-5 figures are not matched.

The Armadillo mesh is unavailable and replaced by a unit sphere proxy (n=900, three sampling modalities); multiplet group means deviate 1.9–3.1% across modalities with divergence growing at higher modes, qualitatively reproducing the claimed phenomenon but not on the paper's asset.

overall: The logbook provides concrete numerical verification for the construction-intrinsic theoretical claims (1–3) through independent re-implementations with discriminating mutations, while honestly identifying a counter-example to the baseline-exclusivity sub-clause of Claim 4. Claims 5–6 are addressed only with synthetic proxies for unavailable data assets, yielding qualitative but not full reproduction.
